agent.problem: This non-opening story card runs to four sentences: the setup with the quoted question, followed by 'With the man RIGHT THERE.', 'In the ROOM.', and 'Within EARSHOT.' The limit is one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The question relies on the unidentified 'they' for who asks Jesus. The preceding story cards do not identify that group either, and they are no longer visible when the baker answers, so the question does not supply its own context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

agent.problem: With 'all' as the right answer, 'some' is also arguably true: healing everyone in the crowd entails healing some of them. A baker could reasonably defend it, so it is not a cleanly false distractor.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

agent.problem: Cards 2, 5, 6 and 7 give no earlier-card basis for choosing their answers: the extent of the healing, what God puts on the Servant, what He proclaims, and whether He quarrels and cries out are all unrevealed details. Four of the stop's seven choice cards are luck-based, including three consecutive guesses at Isaiah's wording, so this stop becomes a guessing game rather than relying mostly on informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
